question: Tell me about Miranda v. Arizona
ground_truth: Supreme Court of the United States
response:
# Miranda v. Arizona (1966)

## The Case
This landmark Supreme Court decision established the requirement that police must inform suspects of their constitutional rights before custodial interrogation.

## Background
Ernesto Miranda was arrested and confessed to crimes during police questioning without being informed of his right to remain silent or consult an attorney.

## The Supreme Court's Ruling
The Court ruled 5-4 that Miranda's confession was inadmissible because police hadn't informed him of his Fifth Amendment protection against self-incrimination and his Sixth Amendment right to an attorney.

## The Miranda Rights
Police must now tell suspects:
- You have the right to remain silent
- Anything you say can be used against you in court
- You have the right to an attorney
- If you can't afford an attorney, one will be provided

## Significance
- Became a cornerstone of criminal procedure
- Protects suspects from coercive police tactics
- Applies to custodial interrogation (when someone isn't free to leave)
- Has been subject to various exceptions and refinements over time

## Impact
While intended to protect suspects, the ruling also standardized procedures that allow police to conduct interrogations legally, making it one of the most debated decisions in criminal justice.
